decision.summary: The Federal Reserve raised the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent.

changes.quote: The Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate.
changes.explanation: The Fed shifted from holding rates steady to raising them by 1/4 percentage point.

changes.quote: While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient.
changes.explanation: The committee noted that consumer spending remains strong despite ongoing global uncertainties.

changes.quote: Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust.
changes.explanation: Business investments and worker productivity continue to perform well.
The statement highlights that inflation is still higher than the central bank's preferred target.

changes.quote: Today's policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal.
changes.explanation: This rate hike is intended to help bring inflation back down to the 2 percent target more quickly.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 20.94% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 5.01% and moved +1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.71% would rise by about $1.99 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 4.1%, and employers added an average of 51k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.7% over the past year (August 2026); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 3%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +7 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.45%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.03% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that future policy choices will depend on incoming economic data regarding growth and price stability. As an educational note, the forecast model gave the next meeting a hold probability of 57% and a hike probability of 42%.
